confidence.rationale: Direct route-to-provider trace shows the key was parsed but did not enter the idempotency store.

findings.remediation: Wrap provider refresh rotation in the shared idempotency store with a key-scoped HMAC principal and reject changed-body reuse.
remediationTests: Concurrent same-key refresh returns one canonical result and one provider call.
Same key with a changed body returns 409.
findings.summary: Repeated or concurrent refresh requests can reach native provider token rotation without returning the first canonical result for the supplied Idempotency-Key.
findings.title: Refresh rotation bypasses the required idempotency store

confidence.rationale: Credential replacement, global logout, and sign-in visibly preceded any durable subject restriction.

findings.remediation: Persist a subject-wide deny-only recovery restriction before any native mutation, then make finalization resumable.
remediationTests: Lost-factor recovery stages restriction before provider credential update.
A different session for the same subject remains restricted after staged failure.
findings.summary: A failure after native credential mutation but before durable recovery finalization can leave the recovered subject able to obtain ordinary access without the required replacement factor.
findings.title: Credential replacement occurs before a durable restriction checkpoint

confidence.rationale: The shared Map allocation path and all eight concrete call sites were reviewed.

findings.remediation: Bound the bucket map, purge expired buckets before allocating, and fail closed at capacity without adding another key.
remediationTests: Expired buckets are evicted before capacity denial.
A new subject is denied at the live-bucket cap and map size does not grow.
findings.summary: Eight Feature-007 route subjects can allocate unique HMAC rate-bucket entries without a global capacity limit or proactive expired-entry eviction.
findings.title: Pre-authentication rate limiter retains unbounded attacker-selected buckets

confidence.rationale: All nine endpoints share the same JWT-only actor wrapper and reach protected sinks without current-session authority.

findings.remediation: Propagate native session_id and require authoritative current-session plus subject-restriction decisions before OTP session return and every protected identity-onboarding operation.
remediationTests: A restricted session is denied before a protected onboarding sink.
A revoked session is denied while its JWT remains cryptographically valid.
findings.summary: Nine protected identity-onboarding reads and mutations verify JWT/profile ownership but omit authoritative auth.sessions current-state and subject-wide recovery-restriction enforcement.
findings.title: Revoked or recovery-restricted JWT reaches nine legacy identity operations

confidence.rationale: The SQL predicate omitted identity verification_status and expires_on while a true result reached credential replacement.

findings.remediation: Require a decided verified case joined to a currently verified, non-expired identity, without inventing a non-canonical freshness duration.
remediationTests: A verified case linked only to a revoked identity is rejected.
A verified case linked only to an expired identity is rejected.
findings.summary: The repeated-proof predicate accepts a verified case without requiring a currently verified and unexpired linked identity.
findings.title: Expired or revoked identity evidence can satisfy lost-factor recovery

confidence.rationale: The restriction lookup required bound_native_session_id while normal login could issue another session for the same subject.

findings.remediation: Enforce the restriction by subject across every session and every protected Core API operation until replacement-factor completion.
remediationTests: A second session for the restricted subject receives mfa_enrollment_only.
Legacy protected onboarding operations deny the subject-wide restricted session.
findings.summary: Recovery restriction is keyed to one native session ID, so the recovered subject can obtain another session that is not restricted.
findings.title: Restricted recovery can be bypassed by issuing a new ordinary session
